issue: Can a sentencing court draw an adverse inference about a defendant's lack of remorse from the defendant's silence without violating the Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination?
provision: U.S. Const. amend. V; Mitchell v. United States, 526 U.S. 314 (1999)

sides.position: Excerpt does not state this side's rule. It notes a circuit split on whether Mitchell's bar on adverse inferences from silence extends to remorse in the capital sentencing context. The positions and the circuits on each side are not identified.
cases: United States v. Caro, 597 F.3d 608 (4th Cir. 2010)
United States v. Sepulveda, 64 F.4th 700 (5th Cir. 2023)

quote: Cf. United States v. Caro, 597 F.3d 608, 629 (4th Cir. 2010) (describing circuit split on whether Mitchell extends to adverse inferences about remorse in the capital sentencing context).
cite: United States v. Sepulveda, 64 F.4th 700 (5th Cir. 2023)
